text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests that measure your average or current blood sugar levels.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests that measure your average or current blood sugar levels

text_blocks.snippet: Doctors use three main tests to diagnose type 2 diabetes:

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar over the past two to three months. You do not need to fast for this test.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures your blood sugar after you do not eat or drink anything (except water) for at least 8 hours.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Checks your blood sugar before and two hours after you drink a special sugary liquid.
Diabetes: 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or higher at the two-hour mark

Random Plasma Glucose Test: If you have classic symptoms of high blood sugar (like extreme thirst, frequent urination, blurry vision, or unexplained weight loss), a random blood sugar level of 200 mg/dL or higher can diagnose diabetes right away.
Repeat Testing: Unless clear symptoms of hyperglycemia are present, doctors usually confirm a positive test result by repeating the test on a separate day.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about official evaluation methods through the American Diabetes Association Diagnosis Guide.
